findings.requirement: R-12 maximum-safe improvement and the stated control-health invariant that every canary/exposure interval has exactly one safe HEALTHY-to-degraded interrupt.

docs/state-transition-manifests.md:825 and 829 leave a reachable exposed CANARY_FAILED interval before IR11-X creates rollback.

docs/state-transition-manifests.md:1053 claims IH01-C/W/WV/A/P/PV/D/O exhaust every active member/effect interval, rejects subsequent progress after degradation, and limits IH05 to no-exposure/no-active-generation tuples.
adversarial_trace: Reach an exposed CANARY_PASSED tuple after IR08 (the same defect also appears in WIDENING_REVIEW, PROMOTION_PENDING_APPROVAL, and the IR09-X->IR11-X gap).
Commit generic IH01, which is legal by its negative rollout guard and changes health to TELEMETRY_DEGRADED without a synchronized rollout/rollback transition.

IH05 cannot restore because exposure and the active generation exist. No IH06 row accepts CANARY_PASSED. IH04 merely says abort/rollback in an effects cell but is not a rollback-entry owner and supplies no rollout/rollback coordinate edge. The invariant rejects ordinary progress after stale health.
findings.impact: A telemetry failure can leave active exposure stopped incompletely or stranded without the required rollback. It also falsifies the plan's material claim that the named active interrupt set is exhaustive.
findings.required_correction: Derive the active/exposure source set from reachable tuples, not the six-state hand list. Add synchronized degraded-state safety rows for CANARY_PASSED, WIDENING_REVIEW, PROMOTION_PENDING_APPROVAL, and the exposed CANARY_FAILED pre-rollback interval (plus any other derived omissions). Each X branch must fence/stop and create or reuse exactly one rollback; N branches need complete protected no-exposure proof. Require exact source-set equality and race degradation before/after each adjacent rollout edge.
